verses: فَقَالَ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ

وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةً وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَيَزْدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِيمَٰنًا وَلَا يَرْتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ وَٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًا كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَمَا هِىَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْبَشَرِ
لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ
بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفًا مُّنَشَّرَةً
وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ هُوَ أَهْلُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ

Only in BD 125 (pYuya): address to the gods, examination, gate names, Thoth, rubric: Self-praise of the just: I gave bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothes to the naked (and a ferry to the boatless); The dwelling or throne of the highest god rests on (primeval) water; Each part of the gate (jambs, lintel, bolt, doorkeeper, floor, even the soles of the feet) refuses passage until the dead says its secret name; The just one's front, back and middle are pure; no limb of his is without Maat; Gate-guardians interrogate the dead: who are you, what is your name, where did you pass, what did you see, what did they give you?; The just one lives on Maat and feeds on Maat; the divine judges too are said to live on Maat, with no lie in their bodies; Rubric formula: 'truly effective, (proven) millions of times'; The dwelling of Osiris has a roof of fire, walls of living uraeus serpents and a floor of flood water; In the judgment of the dead the heart is weighed on a balance against Maat; Anubis checks the plummet and Thoth records the result; The dead declares himself without wrong, without sin and without any witness against him; there is no one he has harmed; The ritual image is drawn in ochre on clean ground on which no pig, goat (or lion, horse) has trodden; Whoever has this book made for him prospers with his children, is a confidant of the king and is turned back at no gate of the West; and 8 more.

leads.title: Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH ↔ The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Measure for measure: as you have done, so it shall be done to you; your deed returns on your head (weight 7.1); The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.1.

Only in Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH: Edom condemned for violence against its brother Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's fall; Exiles of Jerusalem in Sepharad and of Israel as far as Zarephath will repossess the land; The enemy stands at the crossroads to cut off and hand over the fleeing survivors; Prohibition of gloating over, looting or handing over one's brother on the day of his calamity; The house of Jacob will be fire and the house of Esau stubble consumed without survivor; On Mount Zion there will be escape (peletah) and holiness in the coming judgment; Saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingship shall be YHWH's; Conquerors cast lots over a captured city or its nobles; The wicked should drink of the wrath (cup) of Shaddai.

Only in The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen: The people of paradise ask the damned what brought them to hell; they answer: we did not pray, feed the poor, and we denied the day; Those who turn from the reminder are like startled wild asses fleeing from a lion (qaswara); Every soul is held in pledge (rahina) for what it has earned; Each of the deniers wants to be given scrolls unrolled (personally revealed) to him; Over hell are nineteen; its keepers are angels whose number is made a test; God created a man alone, gave him extended wealth and sons present at his side; yet he wants more and stubbornly opposes the signs; The companions of the right (ashab al-yamin, al-maymana) are saved; the companions of the left (al-mash'ama) are damned; The intercession of intercessors will not benefit the damned; no soul has power to help another; How many wardens or demons are set over the underworld or hell [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; The people wash their garments to prepare for God's appearance; You will not will unless God wills; At the judgment the dead state whether they fed the hungry [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.
